title: Endpoint orchestration & integration discovery — Juno Labs
meeting_header: Date: 2026-12-01 | Start: 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~52m | Location: Zoom | Recording: yes
Summary: Initial integration discovery focused on how Juno Labs will route requests between Redwood hosted vs. dedicated vs. private, SDK usage with LangChain/LlamaIndex, gateway/proxy strategy for multi-tenant edge, rate limits/quotas, and observability hooks. Agreement to run a 1-week pilot and exchange security docs and Dedicated pricing.
Topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
SDK integration patterns (Node/Python), LangChain and LlamaIndex adapters
Gateway/proxy vs sidecar deployment for request routing
Rate limits, per-tenant quotas, burst capacity
Observability: tracing hooks, token-level cost breakdowns, traces/metrics
Security: SSO/SAML, KMS integration, SOC2 audit logs
action_items: Maya Patel: Send Dedicated pricing estimate (8x A100 equiv) and pilot pricing (due 2026-12-03)
Carlos Vega: Share sample LangChain/LlamaIndex adapter snippet and example proxy config (due 2026-12-02)
Priya Shah: Provide expected QPS and typical seq lengths for main endpoints (due 2026-12-04)
Maya Patel: Share security pack (SOC2 summary, SSO guide, KMS integration notes) and IP allowlist template (due 2026-12-03)
Tom Rivers: Confirm pilot scope and internal stakeholders for a 1-week evaluation (due 2026-12-07)
next_steps: Set up 1-week dedicated pilot with routing to Redwood Dedicated and fallback to Hosted
Exchange network allowlist and schedule a private deployment feasibility call if pilot needs VPC
Run a perf run: 50 concurrent sessions, 512-token average, measure tail latency and cost per 1k tokens
Provide Redwood sample SDK repo and LangChain wrapper link: https://redwood.link/langchain-adapter
transcript:
00:00 Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone thanks for joining, appreciate you squeezing this in. Quick roll call?
00:05 Evan (Juno): Evan here, hi.
00:06 Priya (Juno): Priya on my side.
:08 Tom (Juno): Tom — sorry joined a bit late, CTO.
00:12 Maya: Great, so agenda — high level integration patterns, SDKs, proxy strategy, quotas/observability, and then next steps. Carlos from our infra team will do the deep technical flyover.
00:22 Carlos (Redwood SE): Hi all, yeah I can start with how customers typically stitch Redwood into an existing API gateway or run a sidecar.
00:30 Evan: Good. Our main question up front — we have internal agents orchestrator that fans requests to different backends. We need to know whether to use Redwood Hosted and fallback to Dedicated, or go straight Dedicated or Private. Latency matters for chat use case, but cost matters too.
00:45 Carlos: Totally. Quick framing — Hosted gives fastest time-to-value; Dedicated gives predictable throughput and VPC options; Private is for air-gapped/regulatory needs. For routing you can do policy-based: latency-first -> hosted, cost-first -> quantized variant on Dedicated, etc.
00:59 Priya: Could you give a concrete example for the gateway? We have an Envoy-based gateway today, does Redwood support a proxy pattern?
01:10 Carlos: Yes — common approach is an adapter proxy in front of your gateway which tags requests and forwards to Redwood endpoints. We provide a small proxy example and an Envoy filter config. The two patterns we see: 1) gateway-proxy: central proxy translates and routes to Hosted/Dedicated, 2) sidecar: per-pod sidecar that talks directly to Redwood. Gateway-proxy is simpler for multi-tenant routing.
01:33 Tom: If we do gateway-proxy, how do we handle tenant-level quotas and rate limits? We need per-customer quotas, and burst protection.
01:41 Maya: Good question. Redwood exposes per-token usage headers and per-route metrics. You can push rate limit decisions into the gateway using token buckets keyed by tenant id. We also support per-api-key quotas from the control plane — useful if you want Redwood to enforce hard caps.
01:55 Evan: Are those quotas enforced in Hosted only or also on Dedicated/Private?
02:01 Carlos: Supported across Hosted and Dedicated — for Private the control plane can still enforce quotas if you run our control plane; otherwise you'll run local enforcement.
02:10 Priya: What about SDKs? We use Python and Node for our app orchestration. Do you have official SDKs and LangChain integrations?
02:18 Maya: Yes, official SDKs for Node/Python, and we have adapters for LangChain and LlamaIndex. Carlos will show a snippet.
02:25 Carlos: (shares link in chat) https://redwood.link/langchain-adapter — example shows a chain that swaps in a Redwood model, handles streaming, and demonstrates how to plug KV cache into persistent store.
02:40 Priya: Nice. We rely on LlamaIndex for retrieval-augmented generation; does Redwood support memory / KV caching for RAG?
02:49 Carlos: Absolutely. Our serving runtime supports KV cache and prefix caching; the LangChain/LlamaIndex adapters expose hooks to prewarm cache per-user or per-doc. Caution: if you want cross-tenant shared cache you need to partition keys.
03:03 Evan: One of our pain points previously was long tail latency — can you talk about batching vs latency SLOs?
03:12 Carlos: Sure. We do continuous batching; you can set latency SLOs per-route. If you set a strict latency SLO we prioritize small batches and fall back to an unquantized model variant to hit tail latency. The tradeoff is higher cost per token; if you relax SLO you get higher batching and lower cost.
03:31 Tom: For the pilot we need to measure cost and 95/99th latencies. Any recommended test plan?
03:38 Carlos: Run a 50-concurrent client load, average 512 tokens, spike to 200 QPS, capture 95th/99th over 30 minutes. We'll supply a benchmark harness.
03:50 Maya: We'll put that in the next steps and include a spreadsheet so you can compare hosted vs dedicated numbers.
04:00 Priya: Security — SOC2, SSO, KMS — do you have SOC2, and can we integrate with our KMS?
04:08 Maya: We are SOC2 Type 2. We support SAML SSO for Console and API-level role mapping, and we integrate with customer-managed KMS in Dedicated and Private deployments. For Hosted we support customer-managed keys through an HSM integration on request.
04:25 Evan: Audit logs? We need immutable logs for model invocations for compliance.
04:31 Carlos: Audit logs are available — per-request metadata, user id, model id, timestamps. Retention is configurable for Dedicated and Private; Hosted has tiered retention add-ons.
04:42 Priya: Observability hooks — can we get spans/traces into our OpenTelemetry stack?
04:48 Carlos: Yes, there's an observability SDK that emits spans and token-level cost as attributes. We also export metrics via Prometheus and have a tracing export to Jaeger/OTLP.
04:59 Evan: Any friction integrating with our existing tracing? We use OTLP collector.
05:04 Carlos: That should be straightforward — we emit OTLP and you can hook into your collector. We also have lightweight logging webhook for errors.
05:12 (00:05:30) Maya: Quick check — timeline? You mentioned wanting to pilot before year-end?
05:18 Tom: We want internal signoff by mid-December, pilot sponsored by Platform team the week of Dec 7.
05:25 Maya: Cool, pilots are usually a week. We'll prepare a pilot plan.
05:30 Evan: About model variants — do you host both open models and custom finetuned models?
05:36 Carlos: We host open and finetuned variants. If you bring a custom model for Dedicated or Private we can help with onboarding. Also mention quantized variants — good cost savings.
05:46 Priya: For finetuned models, how do rollouts work? Can we canary?
05:50 Carlos: Yes, rollouts: canary, A/B, automatic fallback to stable model variant if unseen regressions. We also tie quality regressions to prompt sets/alerts.
06:02 Evan: Network — if we want VPC peering for Dedicated, how long to provision?
06:07 Maya: Typically 3-5 business days once network details and allowlist are provided. Private on-prem takes longer — usually a week+ depending on infra.
06:15 Priya: Does Dedicated support burst capacity? We have periodic spikes when ingestion jobs kick off.
06:20 Carlos: Yes, Dedicated supports burst capacity — configurable. You can reserve baseline and allow bursts via autoscaling policies.
06:28 Tom: About billing — granularity per token is fine but we need visibility per-route for cost allocation.
06:33 Maya: Console provides token-level cost breakdown per api-key/route and you can export cost reports. We'll show you the dashboard in the pilot.
06:43 Evan: We're heavy users of LangChain agents — does Redwood handle function/tool-calling smoothly with streaming?
06:50 Carlos: We support streaming and structured function/tool-calls. The SDK includes helpers for chunked streaming and tool-calls that preserve function metadata.
06:58 Priya: Any out-of-the-box connectors for embedding stores? We use Pinecone today and might migrate to vector DB in future.
07:05 Carlos: We don't host an embedding store but adapters exist for Pinecone, Milvus, and others. We can help with examples.
07:13 Maya: Ok I'm going to stop and take action items — before I do, any blockers you foresee for pilot?
07:20 Evan: Main blocker is security signoffs — need SOC2 and KMS details. Also network allowlist.
07:26 Tom: Also need to confirm internal stakeholders and success metrics: 95th < 350ms for median production path and cost target $X per 1k tokens — we'll fill X once we see numbers.
07:40 Carlos: We'll provide test harness and run baseline numbers for both Hosted and Dedicated; you'll be able to see cost/latency tradeoffs.
07:46 (00:08:10) Priya: One more thing — how intrusive is the proxy? We prefer no extra hop if possible.
07:53 Carlos: Sidecar reduces an extra network hop but increases deployment complexity. Gateway-proxy is low friction and centralized. For low-latency chat we often recommend sidecar per-service; for multi-tenant routing and quotas the gateway-proxy scales nicely.
08:10 Evan: Do you have recommendations for Envoy filter config?
08:14 Carlos: Yes, sample config in the repo I'll share. It shows routing, header enrichment, and per-tenant keys.
08:20 (00:09:00) Maya: Sharing links now: Architecture deck: https://redwood.link/juno-arch, SDK samples: https://redwood.link/sdk-examples.
08:28 Tom: Thanks. A bit of cross talk but got the links.
08:30 (00:09:30) Evan: On the topic of model fallbacks, if Dedicated capacity is saturated, is there automated fallback to hosted?
08:38 Carlos: You can configure a routing policy that fails over to Hosted or to a cheaper quantized variant. We also support region fallback. Automations can be time-based or load-based.
08:47 Priya: For observability, can we tag spans with tenant id and correlation id to stitch user actions end-to-end?
08:54 Carlos: Yes, SDK supports adding correlation_id and tenant_id as attributes on spans and metrics; console dashboards can slice by those keys.
09:03 Maya: Ok we're at 35 minutes in — let's recap next steps and ownership.
09:08 Maya: Action item recap: pricing + security pack from me, SDK examples and proxy configs from Carlos, pilot metrics and spreadsheet, and internal confirmation from Juno.
09:18 Tom: We'll aim to confirm pilot participants by Dec 7.
09:22 Evan: We'll send Priya's load profile and seq lengths.
09:25 Priya: Will do — I'll put together typical qps and payload distributions.
09:28 (00:36:00) Carlos: One small gotcha — if you plan to store KV cache cross-tenant, you'll need to ensure encryption separation; we recommend tenant-scoped key prefixes.
09:36 Tom: Noted.
09:38 Maya: Any other competitors or vendor constraints?
09:40 Evan: We're also talking to Anthropic for comparison but your batching and observability story is compelling.
09:46 Maya: Great — we'll send the security docs and a sample pilot plan by Friday.
09:50 (00:40:00) Priya: Quick perf note — our model prompts average 480 tokens but sometimes spike to 1,200; include that in tests.
09:56 Carlos: We'll parameterize token lengths in the harness.
10:02 Maya: Ok last thing — can we get SSO set up for the console before pilot so our team can view dashboards?
10:08 Maya: (to Tom) If you send the SAML metadata we'll set up a test org.
10:12 Tom: Will send by EOD tomorrow.
10:15 Maya: Perfect. Thanks everyone, we'll follow up by email with links and dates.
10:20 Evan: Thanks all.
10:22 (crosstalk) Meeting end.
